mechanical.notes: 0 guard failures; boot clean; negative control 9/9; budget 612/1200 draws. Textures are DataTexture (offline-first applies to textures as to geometry), deterministic by integer hash not a stateful PRNG (so two attempts stay comparable). THE FINDING THAT MATTERS: a guard was DEFENDING A WRONG DECISION. verifyLuminairesKeepTheirOwnHue asserted sign -1 on ceiling_daylight — it REQUIRED the cold panel the reference contradicts. Its FORM was correct (does the declared identity survive the tone curve?) but its DECLARED IDENTITY was false, so it fired correctly on the wrong white and every green run CONFIRMED THE ERROR WITH GROWING CONFIDENCE. This is distinct from the dead guard (never fires) and the NaN guard (always green): a guard can only check consistency with a DECLARED intention, never the CORRECTNESS of that intention, because it has no access to the reference — and adding more guards makes it WORSE, multiplying the confirmations. Only the photo breaks the loop. Its separation rule was also reformulated to a ZONE property (two luminaires in different rooms may share a colour — it would otherwise have failed the warm aisle panel against a warm lounge downlight it is never seen beside; the sixth time the fix was the criterion, not the design). And a texture changes what a pixel guard must measure: a colour MAP multiplies the material colour, so verifyNoSurfaceRendersAsAHole judging m.color alone would read every textured surface as brighter than it renders — silently optimistic right as this pass lands; each generator now records its meanFactor (plank 0.850, carpet 0.825, ceiling 0.956) and the guard applies it (verified not decorative: forcing the floor map to 0.03 fires the guard at luma 4.6).

notes: Inline orchestrator judgment. The surface pass corrected three things only the photo could settle — the floor is wood plank not raised-floor tile (caught by looking BEFORE building), the ceiling panels are warm sunlight not cold daylight, and the door LEDs vary by cabinet — all via the assets' own declared options, never a scene-authored material. The standout is the deepest of the run's three guard-failure kinds: a guard with the right FORM but a false DECLARED PREMISE fires correctly on the wrong value, so every green run confirms the error with growing confidence and more guards only multiply the confirmations — a guard checks consistency with an intention, never the correctness of the intention, and only the reference breaks the loop. Textures are offline DataTextures, the pixel-hole guard now accounts for a colour map's mean factor, and the 9/9 negative control holds. Cleared to the lighting-camera pass.
